about: Ohio grant programs with their own application windows that aren't posted on the Ohio Grants Partnership list, entered by hand from each program's own page: the Commission on Minority Health's grants, the Attorney General's crime victim funds, the Ohio History Fund, and the OneOhio Recovery Foundation's regional grants. grantmatch/local.py checks this file and turns each entry into an Ohio program record; the weekly page watcher rereads every page. Change an entry only from the official page, and update its checked date.

programs.title: Minority Health Month Grants
programs.objectives: Small grants for health awareness and disease prevention events during April, Minority Health Month, for economically disadvantaged racial and ethnic minority communities in Ohio. Each grantee holds at least two educational events on two separate days in April, in person or online.
programs.who: Public or private organizations with 501(c)(3) status at the time of application (pending status doesn't count), serving or located near economically disadvantaged minority communities. One application per organization. Individuals and national organizations (other than local chapters) can't apply.
programs.application: Apply in the Commission's Minority Health Grants Management (MHGM) system; the round's RFP and recorded help sessions are on the Annual Grants page. Upload your IRS 501(c)(3) letter, W-9, liability insurance and an event form for each event. At least 20% of project funds must come from other sources (in-kind counts).
programs.award: The Commission's page lists $3,500 per applicant; earlier FY27 rounds offered up to $4,000. Paid as reimbursement after the events.
programs.deadlines: Round 5 for April 2027 events opens November 2, 2026 and closes December 4, 2026. A new set of rounds opens each year.
programs.subjects: Health; Minority health; Health equity; Prevention; Health education; Community events

programs.title: Miscellaneous Supplemental Grants (health screenings and conferences)
programs.objectives: One-time grants for large health screenings or one- or two-day health conferences that focus on minority health disparities and reach Ohioans from at least two counties. Not for ongoing programs or fundraising.
programs.who: Public or private organizations with 501(c)(3) status at the time of application, serving or near minority communities. City and county health departments can't apply for large health screening funds.
programs.application: Apply in the Commission's MHGM system at least 90 calendar days before the event, with no exceptions. Upload your IRS 501(c)(3) letter, liability insurance and compliance form; a CPA audit is needed for the larger amount. At least 20% of project funds must come from other sources.
programs.award: Up to $15,000, or up to $25,000 for larger screenings and conferences that reach more counties.
programs.deadlines: Open all year while funds last; apply at least 90 days before the event.
programs.subjects: Health; Minority health; Health screening; Conferences; Health equity

programs.title: Ohio History Fund Grants
programs.objectives: Competitive matching grants for local history, prehistory and historic preservation in three categories: Bricks & Mortar (buildings listed on the National Register or protected by a local preservation ordinance), Programs & Collections, and Organizational Development.
programs.who: Ohio nonprofit organizations in good standing with the Secretary of State, and public entities such as local governments, public libraries and schools. For-profits, individuals and current History Fund grantees with open projects can't apply.
programs.application: Read the History Fund guidelines, create an account in the Ohio History Connection grant portal, and submit with the work schedule, budget and signature forms. Paper and emailed applications aren't accepted.
programs.award: $2,000 to $20,000 for Bricks & Mortar and Programs & Collections projects; Organizational Development grants are smaller. Matching funds, goods or services are required.
programs.deadlines: Once a year, on the second Tuesday of September: September 14, 2027. Awards are announced in mid-February.
programs.contact: Ohio History Connection History Fund staff, listed on the page
programs.subjects: History; Historic preservation; Museums; Archives; Libraries

programs.title: VOCA and SVAA Crime Victim Assistance Grants
programs.agency: Ohio Attorney General, Crime Victim Services Section
programs.objectives: Grants to crime victim assistance programs from the federal Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) and Ohio's State Victims Assistance Act (SVAA) funds, for direct services to victims of crime.
programs.who: Crime victim assistance programs run by public and nonprofit agencies in Ohio. The Guidelines and Eligibility document on the page gives the full rules.
programs.application: Apply through the Attorney General's grant management system when a cycle opens; the subrecipient manual, quick start guide and eligibility guidelines are on the page.
programs.deadlines: One application cycle a year. The 2026-2027 cycle is closed; watch the page for the next one.
programs.subjects: Crime victims; Victim advocacy; Domestic violence; Sexual assault; Safety

programs.title: Ohio Rape Crisis Trust Fund
programs.agency: Ohio Attorney General, Crime Victim Services Section
programs.objectives: Annual funding for qualifying Ohio rape crisis programs.
programs.who: Qualifying Ohio rape crisis programs; the page and its guidelines describe who qualifies.
programs.application: Apply through the Attorney General's grant management system when the year's application opens.
programs.deadlines: Applications typically open in mid-May, with award notices at the end of June.
programs.subjects: Sexual assault; Crime victims; Rape crisis; Victim advocacy

programs.title: OneOhio Regional Grants (opioid settlement)
programs.agency: OneOhio Recovery Foundation (created by the state to distribute 55% of Ohio's opioid settlement funds)
programs.objectives: Regional grants for prevention, treatment, recovery and community resilience work for people with any substance use disorder, or affected by a family member's, including co-occurring mental health conditions. Each of OneOhio's 19 regions recommends its own awards.
programs.who: Organizations registered with the Ohio Secretary of State under their current EIN for two consecutive years; out-of-state organizations that operate in Ohio and are registered here can also apply. Each cycle's RFP gives the full rules.
programs.application: Submit a funding inquiry in the Foundation's grant portal during a cycle's window; selected applicants are invited to a full technical application.
programs.award: Cycle 2 made $45.8 million available across the 19 regions. Each cycle's RFP sets request sizes.
programs.deadlines: Cycle 2 took funding inquiries from January 14 to February 11, 2026 and is closed. Watch the page for the next cycle.
programs.contact: OneOhio Recovery Foundation, through the grants page
programs.subjects: Substance use; Addiction; Recovery; Prevention; Treatment; Mental health; Families
